source_title: NZ vs IND: Diwali comes early as Abhishek 113 helps India chase 199 in 13.2 overs - India Today
source_excerpt:
NZ vs IND, 3rd T20I: Abhishek Sharma smashed a 38-ball 113 and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blasted 45 off 19 deliveries as India chased 199 in 13.2 overs, setting a powerplay world record and taking an unassailable 3-0 series lead.
Brief Scores: India (199 for 4 in 13.2 overs) beat New Zealand (198/3 in 20 overs) by 6 wickets to seal a 3-0 lead in the five-match series. Scorecard | Highlights
Diwali, the festival of fireworks, arrived two weeks early in Wellington as India produced one of the most explosive displays of big-hitting in a T20I contest. Abhishek Sharma smashed a 38-ball 113 after teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blazed his way to 45 off just 19 deliveries as India chased down 199 in 13.2 overs on Tuesday. The batting blitz not only secured a commanding victory but also handed India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.
The build-up to the third T20I in Wellington had been dominated by the gusty winds sweeping through the city. On the eve of the contest, India's players had struggled to cope with the conditions, finding it difficult to keep their hats and caps on during fielding practice as the wind threatened to sweep them away.
But the gusts were nothing compared to the storm Abhishek and Sooryavanshi unleashed during the chase on Tuesday evening. India raced to 50 in just 2.2 overs, brought up their hundred in five overs and finished the powerplay with a staggering 118 runs, setting a world record for the highest team total in the first six overs of a men's T20I.
Abhishek brought up his fourth T20I hundred with one of the most ruthless innings of his career, taking the attack to New Zealand's bowlers from the outset. None of the hosts' new-ball options were spared as Jacob Duffy, Adam Milne and Kyle Jamieson were all taken to the cleaners by the Indian openers. Sooryavanshi, promoted to open in place of Sanju Samson, matched his senior partner's aggression, turning the chase into a relentless assault that left New Zealand scrambling for answers.

Abhishek reached his hundred in just 35 deliveries, five balls slower than his own world record for the fastest T20I century. He finished with 11 sixes and nine fours, sending the ball soaring into the Wellington evening and giving the crowd plenty to cheer about. The spectators who braved the biting cold and gusty conditions to watch a midweek evening contest were rewarded with a spectacular exhibition of power-hitting. Abhishek has now scored nine T20I half-centuries in fewer than 20 deliveries, the most by any batter. He also has two hundreds in fewer than 35 balls, including a 30-ball century against Afghanistan in Delhi earlier this year, the fastest by a batter from a Full Member nation in T20I cricket.
Abhishek came close to breaking his mentor Yuvraj Singh's record for the fastest T20I fifty by an Indian, but fell three deliveries short of the 12-ball milestone. That prompted a cheeky jibe from Yuvraj on Instagram .
Responding to the tease, Abhishek acknowledged the difficulty of matching his mentor's feat, which remains the fastest T20I fifty by an Indian batter.
"I mean, I've said this before as well. I don't know what cricket he was playing back at that time, but it's not that easy at all. And I would say if any batter wants to go there and bat like that, it's not easy at all. You can't just go and score 50 off 12 balls. It just happens once in a while. But, obviously, as a batter, we don't go for that milestone," he said.
Yuvraj, however, later took to X to highlight the scale of Abhishek's achievement, joking about his inability to match the opener's extraordinary scoring rate.
"And I can't score a hundred off 30 or 34 balls. Well played, Abhishek! Great innings, and you even managed to take some singles! Brilliant effort at the other end by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi! A devastating combination! Hats off to Sanju Samson for batting at No. 3 and putting the team first! Well bowled by our bowlers to keep the opposition under 200! A great series win. Congratulations, Team India," Yuvraj wrote. Screengrab from X
As Yuvraj pointed out, India promoted Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to open alongside Abhishek Sharma, pushing Sanju Samson down to No. 3. The move paid off spectacularly, with Abhishek and Sooryavanshi adding 133 runs off just 43 deliveries to turn the chase into a walk in the park.
India, however, lost some momentum after Abhishek fell in the 10th over. Needing just 21 more runs, Samson and Shreyas Iyer struggled to replicate the fluency and aggression of the openers. The brief slowdown did little to threaten the outcome, though, as India completed the chase with 40 deliveries to spare. DISCIPLINED BOWLING SHOW
New Zealand rode on Daryl Mitchell's unbeaten 89 to post 198 for 3 against India in the third T20I in Wellington on Tuesday, but a disciplined finish from the Indian bowlers ensured the hosts did not run away with an even bigger total. Arshdeep Singh was among India's better performers, taking 1 for 33 in his four overs as the visitors restricted New Zealand to 52 runs in the final five overs.
India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl, and Arshdeep made an immediate impact by dismissing Tim Seifert, who fell after playing an indiscreet shot. However, New Zealand recovered through Finn Allen and Mitchell, who counter-attacked with an 86-run partnership for the second wicket.
Allen struck 40 off 25 balls, giving the innings momentum before Nitish Kumar Reddy removed him. Mitchell, meanwhile, held the innings together, combining measured strokeplay with powerful hitting to keep the scoreboard moving.
With Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs unavailable to make a major contribution early in the innings, Mitchell took responsibility for accelerating through the middle and death overs. He found a valuable partner in Jacobs, who remained unbeaten on 39 off 23 deliveries. Their partnership helped New Zealand maintain a strong scoring rate after Allen's dismissal.
Mitchell finished with an unbeaten 89 off 52 balls, his highest T20I score, striking boundaries regularly to ensure New Zealand approached the 200-run mark. Jacobs provided the late impetus, allowing the hosts to finish on 198 for 3.
However, even a total of 198 proved nowhere near enough to challenge India's explosive batting line-up.
The two teams will meet in the fourth T20I on Friday in Auckland, and India will be now be eyeing a sweep of the series. - Ends
